newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees under month more delay on London Club.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees under month more delay on London Club.

text.p: Russia will further delay the announcement of the closing agreement with the London Club of commercial banks-creditors by a period of less than one month, a senior Finance Ministry official said.

"The delay will be less than a month, compared with what was previously expected," Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters. Market sources have said they expected the announcement at the start of October.
Kasyanov said he expected the volume of fully reconciled debt to reach over 50 percent by the end of the week.
"Unfortunately, the sum is lower than we wanted to see by this time," he said.

Vneshbonds, which now represent Russia's debt, are traded on a when-and-if basis, meaning investors get their money only after the agreement is closed. After the closing, Russia will issue new paper, which will make the world's biggest single Brady bond, investors say.

Kasyanov said that Vneshekonombank, the government's agent for the debt, had reconciled over 90 percent of the debt but that only 65 percent of creditors had replied. He said that from August, the Finance Ministry would make weekly statements on how reconciliation was proceeding.
